and were converted to Christianity.
And they requested for themselves Moses the monk as bishop,
and this was granted to them by the order of Valens.
And the Goths and the Iberians came out into the land of the Romans,
and took captive the Scythians (or Scythia?), Moesia, Thrace, Macedonia, Achaia, and all of Hellas.
Valens, being in Constantinople, held back from battle,
because he was afraid of the Goths and Iberians.
The whole populace, however, cried out,
"Give us weapons,
and we will fight!"
And the emperor became angry and went forth, threatening,
"When I return,
I will plow up the city with a team of oxen in exchange for its insolence!"
And when he went,
he was defeated and fled to a certain farmstead (agourros).
And when the barbarians surrounded him,
he hid in an outbuilding
and buried himself in straw.
And when the Goths did not find him,
they set fire to the entire farmstead,
and he was burned.
After Valens, Gratian, the son of Valentinian, [reigned] one year.
He, having already been made autocrat in Rome in the days of his father,
took hold of the empire after Valens.
And he was righteous, chaste, and orthodox in faith,
and not an Arian like his father and his uncle.
And he took for himself as a partner in the empire the great Theodosius from Hispania,
an Iberian by race.
Because this Theodosius had taken care and previously proclaimed Gratian emperor before the burning of Valens.
And at that time a certain Maximus treacherously killed Gratian in Rome,
and made Valentinian, his younger brother, reign in Rome.
After this, sixteen years.
When Gratian was killed {OCR?} and his brother Valentinian the Second {OCR?} reigned in Rome,
Theodosius reigned alone in Constantinople and in all the East.
And he was mighty, wise, and experienced in wars,
and easily conquered the barbarians who were in Thrace.
And in his second year Ardashir died,
and Shapur his son arose after him for four years.
And in his fifth year, Varhran Kirman-Shah reigned over the Persians for twelve years.
And that Theodosius together with Valentinian jointly marched against the tyrant who had killed Gratian,
and killed him,
and both of them entered Rome in triumph.
